groups.when: Work with your Ouro agent from a coding tool: talk to it, hand it work, report back, and read its state.
Install, start, stop, update or inspect the Ouro runtime itself on this machine, and find commands.
Choose, credential and test the model providers each agent lane thinks with, and connect integrations.
Unlock, inspect and change the encrypted store holding an agent's secrets and machine config.
Manage the people an agent knows, their trust and linked accounts, and its live conversations.
Look inside an agent: its private runtime turns and state, attention queue, work board, and wake it.
Reach, import and maintain an agent's email: browser address, MBOX imports, index rebuilds, cleanup.
Connect coding tools to agents: MCP servers they serve or call, editor hooks and plugins.
Let an agent work with other agents: publish its card, onboard peers, message them, and grant them trust.
Keep an agent's work records: tasks, tracks, lessons and friction in its desk, plus Hosted Desk accounts.
Place an agent across machines and channels: rosters and failover, voice calls, and its iMessage host.
Run and administer Shepherd, which keeps an agent's coding sessions: chat, status, pauses and mandates.
Run an agent's RSVP habit: check it, move it off the legacy sender, refresh and send its report.
Change a domain's DNS records and certificate from a binding file, safely: back up, plan, apply, verify, roll back.
Schedule, test and look back at the recurring jobs an agent runs on its own, and wake it early.
Start an agent's daemon, worker or sense process directly with node, as ouro up does, mostly to debug one.
Run the Sanctuary host's root jobs: the Telegram authority, its lifecycle steps, host supervisor and health probes.
Inspect, audit, evaluate or repair saved sessions, nerves events and evaluation suites offline, outside the daemon.
Read, find and change files in the agent's home: open one, list a folder, search names or text, write or edit.
Run commands on the agent's machine: one shell line now, or a long one in the background you check and tail.
Read the public web: search for pages on a subject, or fetch one page by its address as plain text.
Hand coding work to a separate claude or codex worker, then watch it, answer it or stop it.
Act inside the chat a turn came from: react to a message, pick where the reply lands, send a file.
Control the live phone or voice call a turn belongs to: play a sound into it or hang it up.
Learn how to do something: list and load skill guides, or ask Claude Code a read-only question.
Keep and recall what the agent has learned: write diary entries, search them, read recent ones.
Know the people the agent talks with: list them, read one person's record, save what you learn about them.
Help with travel during a turn: weather, country advisories, places, flight offers and bookings, and the private trip ledger.
Keep secrets and personal details in the agent's own vault during a turn: logins, new passwords, profile fields, setup.
Answer questions about an event's guest list during a turn, from a saved RSVP snapshot file.
Reach your owner's Microsoft 365, Teams and raw Azure DevOps APIs: look up the right endpoint, read, change, or message someone.
Plan and tidy an Azure DevOps backlog: list it, file epics and issues, move items, and check the tree for mistakes.
Look after the Sanctuary home server as its Butler: read app, drive, space and download health, and restart or resume with approval.
Watch and steer the coding agents in this machine's terminals for the human, and keep what Shepherd learned from them.
Fix the agent's own bundle git state: set up the repository and remote, make the first commit, and sync it safely.
Run the coding sessions and chats in this Mac's GitHub Copilot app: list, read, message, start, answer, archive and schedule them.
Unstick the agent's own runtime during a turn: revive one stuck sense, or restart the whole daemon as a last resort.
Stop one of the agent's recurring habits during a turn, when the person who started the turn asks for it.
Read or change the household steward's policy during a turn, under the owner's own authenticated request.
Join up an agent's conversations already under way, so shared work in one is visible from the others.
Read and answer the agent's email inside a turn: check, search, open, draft, send, and sort unknown senders.
Wait on something that happens later, like a reply or a delivery: file the wait, record each check, or drop it.
Work with photos, voice notes and documents people sent: find one, get it as a file on disk, or ask about an image.
Spend money for a family member during a turn: approve a checkout, then make a virtual card, and audit what happened.
Track a change to the agent's own harness during a turn: capture friction as a case, decide, verify, deliver, ratify, close.
See and change the agent's own settings in agent.json, with defaults, effects and allowed values.
Settle an external event the agent was woken for: record what it means and whether the owner hears.
Keep track over time: recall and mark turning points, watch cares, jot intentions, see who is around.
See and reach the agent's other chats: live work across sessions, habit runs, transcripts, cross-chat messages.
Get your bearings in a turn: see what a terse or corrective message refers to, and drop stale held work.
Pace a turn: tell the person something midway, give the final answer, stay quiet, close a private turn, or save a question for later.
Hand a failure you can't get around to the engineers: a local failure report, or a GitHub issue.
